title: UFO programs hidden under the Department of Energy

tellings.quote: because I was told I think it was Chris Melon was telling me this that they hide things because anything nuclear would be national security.
SEC. 141. POLICY.—It shall be the policy of the Commission to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security.

r. The term 'Restricted Data' means all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but shall not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to section 142.

plain: The claim is that the government hides its UFO programs inside the Department of Energy, because anything labelled nuclear is automatically national security and so stays secret. Michels says he was told this, he thinks by a man named Chris Mellon, and he links it to the nuclear secrecy law. He does not say which law he means. If it is the Atomic Energy Act, passed by Congress on 30 August 1954, that act made it the policy of the Atomic Energy Commission, the body that came before today's Department of Energy, 'to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security.' The act defines Restricted Data as 'all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons' and the making and use of nuclear material. So the law itself builds the wall of nuclear secrecy Michels describes. Whether UFO programs were ever put behind that wall is his step, and the act neither says so nor rules it out. If true, it would mean the most secret UFO work sits under an energy agency rather than the military.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which law he means; if it is the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, it makes it the policy of the Atomic Energy Commission, the forerunner of today's Department of Energy, "to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security", Restricted Data being "all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons", the nuclear secrecy the teller says things are hidden behind. That UFO programs were hidden under that authority is the teller's step, which the act neither states nor excludes.
